description.value: A prospective clinical study evaluating whether early-phase [18F]-florbetaben PET acquisitions provide quantitative and visual information comparable to FDG PET in patients with clinical suspicion of neurodegenerative dementia.

spans.text: Therefore, we investigated the performance of early acquisitions of [ F]-florbetaben (FBB) PET compared to [ F]-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) PET in a clinical setting.

description.value: Prospective clinical study in which patients with clinical suspicion of dementia underwent early- and late-phase FBB PET and additional FDG PET, with less than 12 months between FBB and FDG PET.

spans.text: The primary objective of the prospective study is the clinical utility of FBB-PET (N = 93 subjects), and in a subset of 33 patients early-phase FBB acquisitions could be performed.

spans.text: The present study demonstrates that the initial [ F]-florbetaben uptake correlates both relative quantitatively and visually highly with FDG images, irrespective of the particular amyloid status.
A total of 83 grey matter volumes of interest (VOIs) predefined in the Hammers atlas ( Hammers et al., 2003 ) were applied to the spatially normalized early-phase amyloid and FDG PET images.
The primary objective of the prospective study is the clinical utility of FBB-PET (N = 93 subjects), and in a subset of 33 patients early-phase FBB acquisitions could be performed.
All cortical brain regions showed highly significant correlations irrespective of the early-phase FBB time frame or the particular reference region (p < 0.0001).

value: The regional pattern of the perfusion surrogate in early-phase FBB images resembles the FDG uptake pattern
The visual assessment of early-phase FBB PET demonstrates the comparability of early-phase FBB and FDG 3D-SSP images

spans.text: In summary, the results of visual assessment in the present study demonstrate the comparability of early-phase FBB and FDG 3D-SSP images.

Regional abnormalities (hypoperfusion/hypometabolism) in FBB  and FDG images were graded as not relevant = 0, low = 1, moderate = 2 and severe = 3 in the following regions: frontal right and left, temporo-lateral right and left, parietal right and left, posterior cingulate/precuneus for both hemispheres.

The visual assessment of all target regions in all 33 patients showed a Spearman's rank correlation coefficient between FBB  and FDG of R  = 0.70 for reader 1, R  = 0.77 for reader 2 and R  = 0.75 for reader 3 (mean R  = 0.74) ( Fig. 3 ).
The regional pattern of the perfusion surrogate in early-phase FBB  images resembles the FDG uptake pattern, as can be seen both in an amyloid-positive and amyloid-negative case.

For visual interpretation of early-phase FBB PET (FBB ) and FDG PET images, three-dimensional stereotactic surface projections (3D-SSP) ( Minoshima et al., 1995 ) were generated using the software Neurostat (Department of Radiology, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, U.S.A.).

For visual interpretation of early-phase FBB PET (FBB ) and FDG PET images, three-dimensional stereotactic surface projections (3D-SSP) ( Minoshima et al., 1995 ) were generated using the software Neurostat (Department of Radiology, University of Washington, Seattle, WA, U.S.A.).
For visual analysis, the intra-reader correlations between hypoperfusion in early-phase FBB and hypometabolism in FDG images were calculated by Spearman's rank correlation coefficient (R ).
